summary.headline: Glottis Q2 FY27 revenue from operations rose 28.8% YoY to Rs 2,765 million, with EBITDA-level margin of about 1.2% (profit Rs 34 million).
summary.overview: Revenue from operations for Q2 FY27 was Rs 2,765 million, up 28.8% YoY and 17.9% QoQ, with other income of Rs 19 million and total income of Rs 2,783 million. Management said exports grew 344.4% YoY and now contribute about 42% of revenue, while logistics fell to about 50% share of revenue from 81%. Margin pressure from operating costs persisted, with profit of Rs 34 million at a 1.2% margin, and top-5 customer concentration fell to about 33% from 41%. The call was largely qualitative; several figures in the transcript are garbled by transcription and were not verified.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 2,151 million in Q2 FY26
Management cited pressure on margins from operating costs
Export revenue up 344.4% YoY; was about 12% a year earlier

financial_highlights.metric: Logistics / home appliances share of revenue

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export revenue grew 344.4% YoY and contributed about 42% of total revenue, up from about 12% a year earlier. Management said it is focusing more on export business alongside import operations.

segments.name: Logistics (import-led)
segments.commentary: Logistics share of revenue moderated to about 50% from 81% in the year-ago quarter; import revenue reportedly grew 16.9% YoY. Share figures in the transcript are partly inconsistent.

segments.name: Home appliances
segments.commentary: Home appliances accounted for about 18% of revenue versus 11% a year earlier.

segments.name: Renewable energy
segments.commentary: Renewable energy share fell to about 16% of revenue from 46% a year earlier, per management.

segments.name: Chemicals and automobiles
segments.commentary: Chemicals contributed about 7% and automobiles about 5% of revenue, with revenue up 532% and 110% YoY respectively. Engineering products about 10%.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Asia contributed about 80% of revenue in Q2 FY27, North America about 11%, and the balance South America, Australia and other markets.

guidance_outlook: Management said it is very bullish on revenue growth and expects growth to be strong, with a reference to a 'double' (likely double-digit) growth, though no specific figure was given for FY27 or FY28.
Management said the challenge is sustaining and increasing bottom-line profitability, and that measures are being worked on.
Management expects crude-linked cost relief if crude settles near USD 70-80/bbl, citing a positive trend for profitability over the next two quarters; no quantified EBITDA guidance.
Container deployment expected to start from Q3 FY27; capex programme targeted to complete during FY27.

Warehousing and transportation margins expected to be double-digit, per management; subsidiaries in the US and Malaysia expected to contribute from around Q4 FY27 (Malaysia after property completion in Q3 or Q4).
capex_capacity: Fleet of about 85 vehicles post-deployment, with GPS tracking; plans to deploy vehicles in multiple locations.
Container deployment delayed due to raw material and geopolitical issues; production complete, rollout from Q3 FY27.
Long-term warehousing lease of about 200,000 sq ft, with plans to scale in South and West India.
Plans for more trucks/fleet deployment in different areas; a transport management system with real-time tracking is being developed. Investment amount not disclosed.
Subsidiaries: US subsidiary incorporated in March, operations started last month; Malaysia subsidiary (Glottis Logistics SDN BHD) just incorporated.
demand_pricing: Industry-wide pricing pressure from renewable energy and smaller regional players, per management.
Shipping lines are not offering long-term contracts due to crude volatility and charter availability; shippers and exporters are moving to spot pricing.
Air freight described as more profitable; management expects double-digit QoQ growth in air freight and has added sales teams and branches across India.
Freight rates reportedly up 4-5 times, prompting management to support customers while tightening customer selection.
Trade receivable days around one year per management's answer (figure as transcribed, may be garbled); measures underway to reduce receivables.

qa_highlights.question: Will falling crude prices lift EBITDA and guidance over the next two quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said crude is settling and a positive trend is expected; it cited USD 70-80/bbl as a level that would help the industry. No quantified guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: How is competition shaping up, especially pricing pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the whole industry faces similar pressure, with renewables declining and exports growing, and the company is focusing on verticals with more opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: Are customers committing to long-term contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: No; shipping lines are unwilling to sign long-term contracts given crude volatility and charter availability, so business is spot-driven.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27/FY28 guidance for revenue growth and EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is bullish on revenue growth, expects double-digit growth, and the focus is on sustaining and improving the bottom line; no margin figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Promoter funding: is it short-term and reversible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said promoter funds of about Rs 60 crore (interest at 10%, tenure of 5 years) were taken to support working capital from high freight rates and expansion; it can be partly or fully repaid based on cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Container fleet, utilisation and backward integration?
qa_highlights.answer: Fleet is about 85 vehicles; containers to roll out from Q3 FY27 after delays from raw material and geopolitical issues; backward integration expected to lift margins.

qa_highlights.question: Air freight growth ambitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Air freight is more profitable; management expects double-digit QoQ growth with new sales teams and branches.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of US tariffs and India-US trade deal on US-bound volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave a vague answer, saying demand is growing in some sectors despite tariffs, with minerals and medical supported and automobiles and power transmission more exposed.

risks_watch: Margin compression: profit of Rs 34 million at 1.2% margin, with management still working on bottom-line improvement.
Working capital and promoter funding of about Rs 60 crore; receivables days elevated as freight rates rise.
Spot-market exposure with no long-term shipping contracts; crude volatility and charter availability.
Container rollout delayed to Q3 FY27; execution risk on capex and subsidiary ramp-up in US and Malaysia.
Transcript quality is poor; several figures (margins, segment shares, receivable days) are garbled and should be verified against the filing.
summary.management_tone: Confident on revenue growth and export momentum, but cautious on profitability: management repeatedly framed sustaining the bottom line as the key challenge. Answers on margin, guidance and tariffs were largely qualitative, with few hard numbers.
key_quotes: And now the challenging part for the company is to how to sustain and increase the bottom line.
Air freight is a better profitable business segment for us.

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.label: New product launch

rows.label: Export and new-market ramp via US and Malaysia subsidiaries
rows.why: Exports grew 344.4% YoY to about 42% of revenue, and the US subsidiary began operations last month with Malaysia contributing from Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Promoter funding of Rs 60 crore repayable from cash flow

tone.note: Management was confident on revenue growth and export momentum but cautious on sustaining bottom-line profit at a 1.2% margin, while analysts pushed on margins, guidance and the lack of hard numbers, and the transcript quality was poor.
